- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.77) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If true outcome consistently underperforms model (especially in early days of forecast horizon), apply mean reversion bias: adjust forecast toward recent 5-day average.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.27) and model is rising, reduce forecast by 1–4% to avoid overconfidence in bullish signals.
- For 30-day forecasts, if first 5 days show large negative deviation, assume “early correction” — reduce forecast by 2–5% for days 1–5.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high-low cycles, model tends to lag — adjust forecast to align with sentiment peaks 1–2 days ahead.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, apply downward pressure — reduce by 3–7% depending on sentiment strength.
